description: WHEN OTHER of 9300-GETACCTDATA-BYACCT at app/cbl/COACTUPC.cbl:3736-3743 - the unexpected CICS RESP on the ACCTDAT keyed read, and the case that CLOSES gate G47 for this program. case04 owns the DFHRESP(NORMAL) arm of all three read sites, case05 the DFHRESP(NOTFND) arm of CXACAIX, case06 the DFHRESP(NOTFND) arm of ACCTDAT and case07 the DFHRESP(NOTFND) arm of CUSTDAT; this case owns the third and last arm of the EVALUATE WS-RESP-CD at :3713, on the ACCTDAT site. Its subject is not the branch alone but the MESSAGE that branch composes, because that message is the only place in COACTUPC where a group item wider than its receiver is moved, and the truncation is observable. THE ARM, statement by statement. All three read paragraphs carry an identically shaped WHEN OTHER - 9200 at :3686-3693, 9300 at :3736-3743 and 9400 at :3785-3792 - and each does six things in this order: SET INPUT-ERROR TO TRUE, SET the paragraph's own filter flag to NOT-OK (FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK at :3738 for this one), MOVE 'READ' TO ERROR-OPNAME at :3739, MOVE the file literal TO ERROR-FILE at :3740, MOVE WS-RESP-CD TO ERROR-RESP at :3741, MOVE WS-REAS-CD TO ERROR-RESP2 at :3742, and MOVE WS-FILE-ERROR-MESSAGE TO WS-RETURN-MSG at :3743. The last of those is NOT wrapped in IF WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF, and that asymmetry is deliberate on the source's part rather than an oversight of this reading: every NOTFND arm in the same three paragraphs IS guarded - :3671, :3720 and :3772 - so a NOTFND text can only be written into an empty WS-RETURN-MSG, while a WHEN OTHER text overwrites whatever is there. On this path the distinction has no visible effect, because :2574 SET WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF TO TRUE immediately before the read chain and the field is still spaces when 9300 reaches it, but the unguarded MOVE is reproduced as written rather than regularised into the guarded shape (practice B5). THE COMPOSED 80 BYTES, span by span from the WS-FILE-ERROR-MESSAGE group declaration at :389-408, which is a group of nine 10-level items and is the whole reason this case exists: FILLER PIC X(12) VALUE 'File Error: ' with its trailing space inside the twelve; ERROR-OPNAME PIC X(8) holding 'READ' and therefore four trailing spaces; FILLER PIC X(4) VALUE ' on ' with a leading AND a trailing space; ERROR-FILE PIC X(9); FILLER PIC X(15) VALUE ' returned RESP ' with a leading and a trailing space; ERROR-RESP PIC X(10); FILLER PIC X(7) VALUE ',RESP2 ' with NO leading space and one trailing space; ERROR-RESP2 PIC X(10); and a final FILLER PIC X(5) VALUE SPACES. 12+8+4+9+15+10+7+10+5 = 80, and that total is itself the FILLER-presence check gate G21 asks for - a codec that dropped any one of the four FILLER spans could not reach 80 and could not produce the text pinned here. THE DOUBLED SPACE. ERROR-FILE is PIC X(9) but LIT-ACCTFILENAME at :573-574 is PIC X(8) VALUE 'ACCTDAT ' - eight bytes with a trailing space of its own - so MOVE LIT-ACCTFILENAME TO ERROR-FILE puts seven letters and TWO spaces into the nine-byte span. The sibling literals are shaped the same way: LIT-CUSTFILENAME 'CUSTDAT ' at :575-576 and LIT-CARDXREFNAME-ACCT-PATH 'CXACAIX ' at :581-582. Both spaces are reproduced. Trimming either would shift every following byte and would silently pass a differ that compared trimmed strings, which is exactly why FieldDiffer compares field by field at declared width rather than by equality of trimmed text (gate G17). THE RESPONSE CODES. WS-RESP-CD and WS-REAS-CD are PIC S9(09) COMP at :40-41 and :42-43, and a MOVE of a signed binary integer into an alphanumeric PIC X(10) receiver renders nine unsigned display digits left justified with one pad space - '000000019 ' and '000000000 ' here, which is the same rendering case06 pins as '000000013 ' for a NOTFND. The RESP itself is not free case data: it is common.FileStatus.NOTOPEN = 19, taken from the module's single home for the CICS RESP vocabulary rather than invented, and it is chosen because it is neither DFHRESP(NORMAL) = FileStatus.NORMAL = 0 nor DFHRESP(NOTFND) = FileStatus.NOTFND = 13, so the EVALUATE at :3713 genuinely falls through both named arms to WHEN OTHER. RESP2 is FileStatus.NO_REASON_CODE = 0, declared explicitly rather than left to the harness's default (practice B8). THE TRUNCATION THIS CASE OWNS, in three widths. The group is 80 bytes. WS-RETURN-MSG at :479 is PIC X(75). A COBOL MOVE of an 80-byte alphanumeric into a 75-byte alphanumeric receiver truncates on the RIGHT, so :3743 stores the first 75 bytes and the last five are lost - and the five that are lost are exactly the trailing FILLER PIC X(5), which means the surviving text ends with ERROR-RESP2's own pad space. That is a coincidence of the layout rather than a design, and it is worth stating because it is what makes the loss invisible to the eye and visible only to a width assertion. :2981 then MOVEs those 75 bytes into ERRMSGO OF CACTUPAO, which app/cpy-bms/COACTUP.CPY:650 declares PIC X(78), so three spaces are appended on the way to the screen. All three widths are pinned: the 80-byte composition is asserted by the span arithmetic above, the 75-byte stored value is the prefix, and the 78-byte painted value is what ERRMSGO carries and what the single expectedMessages entry carries on the SCREEN_ERRMSG_78 channel - a channel that exists precisely so a truncated screen text cannot be compared against an untruncated working-storage one. THE FORCED OUTCOME, and how it differs from case06's curation. A NOTFND can be arranged by withholding a row, and case06 arranges one that way - it seeds ACCTDAT from fixture rows 1 through 49 and omits row 0, which is account 00000000001. A NOTOPEN cannot be arranged by any seeding at all: it is a state of the file, not of its contents. This case therefore seeds ACCTDAT from the COMPLETE unmodified fixture, all 50 rows of 300 bytes, so that row 0 IS present and the read fails anyway - which is the sharpest available statement that the arm was reached by the response code and not by absence, and the cleanest separation between this case and case06. The outcome is declared as forcedOutcomes read -> OTHER with resp 19 and resp2 0, using the ParityCase vocabulary rather than a mechanism invented here, and the harness refuses a run that leaves a declared outcome unasked-for, so the declaration cannot quietly fail to fire. THE DEAD GUARD APPLIES HERE TOO, and this case is consistent with case06 on it because the same reading produces the same answer. 9000-READ-ACCT at :3608-3644 guards its third read with IF DID-NOT-FIND-ACCT-IN-ACCTDAT GO TO 9000-READ-ACCT-EXIT at :3627-3629. DID-NOT-FIND-ACCT-IN-ACCTDAT is an 88-level on WS-RETURN-MSG at :499-500 whose VALUE is the literal 'Did not find this account in account master file'. The WHEN OTHER arm writes the 80-into-75 file-error text instead, and :3719 - the only statement that would have SET the condition name - is commented out with an asterisk in column 7. The guard therefore CANNOT fire on this path either, for a second and independent reason: even an uncommented SET would not have been executed by this arm, which contains no SET of that name at all. Execution continues: :3631 MOVEs CDEMO-CUST-ID - the 000000001 the SUCCESSFUL cross-reference read supplied at :3666 - into WS-CARD-RID-CUST-ID, :3633-3634 PERFORMs 9400-GETCUSTDATA-BYCUST which takes WHEN DFHRESP(NORMAL) at :3764-3765 and SETs FOUND-CUST-IN-MASTER, the second dead guard at :3636-3638 does not fire because its SET at :3769 is commented out too, and :3642-3643 PERFORMs 9500-STORE-FETCHED-DATA over an ACCOUNT-RECORD that no read ever filled. Because FOUND-CUST-IN-MASTER is set when the chain returns, :2577-2579 SETs ACUP-SHOW-DETAILS - the program shows account details after a failed account read. THE UNREAD ACCOUNT RECORD. ACCOUNT-RECORD is COPY CVACT01Y at :640, its own 01 group in WORKING-STORAGE and not among the areas INITIALIZE names at :866-868, so a failed EXEC CICS READ INTO(ACCOUNT-RECORD) leaves it holding what COBOL leaves in an uninitialised group: SPACES in every PIC X span and ZERO in every numeric one. That is the same convention case06 adopts and it follows from the read-outcome contract rather than from convenience - common.FileStatus publishes the outcome vocabulary and account.AccountRepository returns a DISCRIMINATED outcome to its caller instead of abending on the caller's behalf, so the receiving group is untouched rather than absent, unfilled rather than null. The observable consequence is asserted in the navigation image, where 9500 at :3805 MOVEs ACCT-ID into CDEMO-ACCT-ID and leaves ELEVEN ZEROS there even though :1815 had already put the valid 00000000001 in from CC-ACCT-ID, and :3810 MOVEs ACCT-ACTIVE-STATUS into CDEMO-ACCT-STATUS and leaves one space. CDEMO-ACCT-ID reading 00000000000 after a request for 00000000001 is the fingerprint of a 9500 that should not have run, and it is asserted here for the same reason case06 asserts it. THE PATH INTO THE READ. EIBCALEN is 1033 - 160 for CARDDEMO-COMMAREA plus 873 for WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA - so the left disjunct of the commarea gate at :880 is false, and CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM is spaces rather than COMEN01C so the right disjunct at :881-882 is false too: the ELSE at :887-892 restores both areas from DFHCOMMAREA. CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT arrives 1, so CDEMO-PGM-REENTER is true and CDEMO-PGM-ENTER is false, and ACUP-CHANGE-ACTION arrives ACUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED. AID DFHENTER passes the validity gate at :906-912 on its first disjunct so the remap at :914-916 does nothing. The order-sensitive EVALUATE TRUE at :921 lands on WHEN OTHER at :996 - not on :927 CCARD-AID-PFK03, not on :964 which needs CDEMO-PGM-ENTER, not on :966 which needs NOT CDEMO-PGM-REENTER, not on :979 or :980 - and that arm performs 1000-PROCESS-INPUTS, 2000-DECIDE-ACTION and 3000-SEND-MAP before leaving by the forward-only GO TO COMMON-RETURN at :1003. 1100-RECEIVE-MAP at :1051-1058 finds ACCTSIDI neither '*' nor SPACES and MOVEs it into CC-ACCT-ID and ACUP-NEW-ACCT-ID-X, then :1060-1062 GO TOes its exit because the details are unfetched, so ACCTSIDI is the only received field there can be. 1200-EDIT-MAP-INPUTS at :1433-1449 edits only the search key, and 1210-EDIT-ACCOUNT at :1783-1817 finds CC-ACCT-ID numeric and CC-ACCT-ID-N non-zero, so its ELSE at :1814-1816 MOVEs CC-ACCT-ID to CDEMO-ACCT-ID and SETs FLG-ACCTFILTER-ISVALID, which is the guard 2000-DECIDE-ACTION tests at :2573 before SETting WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF at :2574 and performing 9000-READ-ACCT at :2575. THE THREE READS IN ONE PASS. 9200-GETCARDXREF-BYACCT at :3654-3662 reads DATASET(LIT-CARDXREFNAME-ACCT-PATH) = CXACAIX with RIDFLD(WS-CARD-RID-ACCT-ID-X) and takes NORMAL, MOVEing XREF-CUST-ID 000000001 and XREF-CARD-NUM 9680294154603697 into the commarea; CXACAIX is an alternate-index PATH over the CCXREF base and is reached through the one CardXrefRepository's alternate-key finder, never a second table or a second repository (gate G45). The live guard at :3620-3622 tests FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK and does not fire. 9300 then reads DATASET(LIT-ACCTFILENAME) = ACCTDAT with the same 11-byte RIDFLD, KEYLENGTH 11, INTO(ACCOUNT-RECORD) LENGTH 300 - and reports RESP 19, which is this case's subject. 9400 reads DATASET(LIT-CUSTFILENAME) = CUSTDAT with a 9-byte RIDFLD INTO(CUSTOMER-RECORD) LENGTH 500 and takes NORMAL. All three EVALUATE WS-RESP-CD statements keep their source WHEN order - NORMAL, NOTFND, OTHER - exactly (gate G30). THE SEED. CXACAIX is seeded from the complete unmodified cardxref.txt, all 50 rows, RAW at 36 bytes and NOT pre-padded: CVACT03Y declares 50 and the fixture omits the trailing FILLER PIC X(14), so the declared CARDXREF_FILLER_PAD_36_TO_50 normalisation supplies the fourteen spaces once, at seed time, before anything decodes a row, and the final-state image is asserted at the copybook's 50 (gate G16, risk R-F). Pre-padding the input would double-pad it. ACCTDAT is seeded from all 50 rows of acctdata.txt and CUSTDAT from all 50 rows of custdata.txt, every row byte-identical to its fixture, so the alternate-key finder and both keyed reads have to discriminate on their keys rather than return the only row present. Nothing is derived, nothing is altered, and app/data/ASCII is not written to: the COBOL, copybook, BMS, JCL, CSD and data trees are the parity oracle and stay read-only (practice B3). THE RECORD EXPECTATIONS. CXACAIX row 48 - the only row in cardxref.txt whose XREF-ACCT-ID is 00000000001, located by scanning the fixture rather than by assumption - is pinned as four fields in app/cpy/CVACT03Y.cpy order plus the complete 50-byte image ending in FILLER PIC X(14) as fourteen spaces, and CUSTDAT row 0 as nineteen fields in app/cpy/CVCUS01Y.cpy order plus the complete 500-byte image ending in FILLER PIC X(168) as one hundred and sixty-eight spaces. Field names are the copybooks' verbatim and FILLER is an addressable span rather than a gap: pinning the fields AND the whole image is what turns the total width into an assertion, and a record missing a FILLER is short by exactly that span (gates G19 and G21). There is deliberately NO ACCTDAT row projection. The row is seeded and is present, but the read did not deliver it, and a row expectation on the read channel would say the opposite of what this case is about; ACCTDAT is instead pinned on the final-state channel at 50 rows of 300 bytes, which says what is true - the file holds all 50 real records, including 00000000001, and none of them changed. THE SCREEN, from the five rules 3000-SEND-MAP applies at :2650-2661. 3100-SCREEN-INIT MOVEs LOW-VALUES to CACTUPAO at :2669 and assigns the six header items at :2673-2690. 3200-SETUP-SCREEN-VARS takes its ELSE at :2702 because the context is REENTER, and because CC-ACCT-ID-N is not zero the ELSE at :2706-2707 echoes CC-ACCT-ID into ACCTSIDO as 00000000001 - the account the operator asked for is still shown. Its order-sensitive EVALUATE at :2710-2724 lands on WHEN ACUP-SHOW-DETAILS at :2715 rather than on :2711 or :2712, so 3202-SHOW-ORIGINAL-VALUES runs and 3201-SHOW-INITIAL-VALUES never does. 3202's first guard at :2793-2794 is IF FOUND-ACCT-IN-MASTER OR FOUND-CUST-IN-MASTER - OR, not AND - and the customer flag IS set, so the sixteen account moves at :2795-2826 run over the unread record: ACSTTUSO one space, the nine date components four and two spaces each, AADDGRPO ten spaces, and the five monetary items each rendered through WS-EDIT-CURRENCY-9-2-F PIC +ZZZ,ZZZ,ZZZ.99 at :371 as '+           .00' - the sign forced, all nine Z positions suppressed because the integer part is zero and both insertion commas blanked with them, and the two fraction positions surviving because the mask ends .99 and not .ZZ, giving exactly the 15 characters ACRDLIMI declares. The customer guard at :2827-2864 paints the twenty-six ACUP-OLD-CUST items from the real row with the width-driven truncations the fixture forces: ACSZIPCO PIC X(5) keeps 12546 of a PIC X(10) source, ACUP-OLD-CUST-SSN-X is split by reference modification at :2829-2831 into 020, 97 and 3888, the two phone numbers by :2846-2857 into 908/119/8310 and 373/693/8684 from the first thirteen bytes of their 15-byte spans, and ACSCITYO takes ACUP-OLD-CUST-ADDR-LINE-3 at :2841 because address line three IS the city on this screen. The six header items, ACCTSIDO, those sixteen, those twenty-six, INFOMSGO, ERRMSGO and the three function-key lines are 6+1+16+26+1+1+3 = 54, so all fifty-four fields are assigned and not one is LOW-VALUES. 3250-SETUP-INFOMSG at :2955-2981 is order-sensitive too and its arm was DERIVED rather than assumed: CDEMO-PGM-ENTER at :2958 is false and ACUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED at :2960 is false because :2578 replaced it, so WHEN ACUP-SHOW-DETAILS at :2962 wins and SETs PROMPT-FOR-CHANGES - WS-INFO-MSG PIC X(40) holding the 39-character literal at :470-471, trailing period included - which :2979 MOVEs into INFOMSGO PIC X(45) right-space-padded to 45. FKEYSO, FKEY05O and FKEY12O are the mapset's own INITIAL text and are never assigned by the program. THE ATTRIBUTE PLANES. :3171-3173 does not fire because CDEMO-LAST-MAPSET is seven spaces rather than the card-list mapset. :3176-3178 DOES fire because FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK was set at :3738, so ACCTSIDC carries DFHRED. :3180-3184 does NOT fire because FLG-ACCTFILTER-BLANK is false, so no '*' is written over ACCTSIDO - red WITHOUT the marker, which is FieldAttributeSetter's rule and the whole of gate G38 on this path: the context IS REENTER so CSSETATY's precondition is satisfied, and the reason only one field is red is that only one thing failed. :3186-3189 then GO TOes 3300-SETUP-SCREEN-ATTRS-EXIT because FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK is set, so all thirty-nine CSSETATY expansions from :3208 onwards are SKIPPED rather than executed as no-ops. Every other colour is therefore the default DFHDFCOL and every highlight the default DFHDFHI, both x'00' exactly as MOVE LOW-VALUES left them, except the information line: 3390-SETUP-INFOMSG-ATTRS at :3566-3571 finds WS-NO-INFO-MESSAGE false - there IS a message - and moves DFHBMASB, a field attribute drawn from a different section of DFHBMSCA than the item's own plane, which is reproduced rather than normalised. FKEY05 and FKEY12 stay hidden because :3573 needs ACUP-CHANGES-MADE and :3578 needs PROMPT-FOR-CONFIRMATION and the state is ACUP-SHOW-DETAILS with the change prompt. The xxxA items 3310 and 3320 write are deliberately NOT declared: they are items of the input redefine CACTUPAI, not of the sent CACTUPAO. THE CURSOR is ACCTSIDL, reached by the SECOND pair of the order-sensitive EVALUATE at :3009 rather than by WHEN OTHER, and the reason is specific to this case's message. FOUND-ACCOUNT-DATA at :3010 is false because 3250 left WS-INFO-MSG holding the change prompt. NO-CHANGES-DETECTED at :3011 is false, and it is false BECAUSE of the text this case composes: that 88-level tests WS-RETURN-MSG for 'No change detected with respect to values fetched.' and WS-RETURN-MSG holds the file-error text instead. WHEN FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK at :3013 is then TRUE, so :3015 MOVEs -1 into ACCTSIDL. COBOL positions the cursor by moving -1 into a symbolic-map length item, so the xxxL item IS the cursor. THE NEXT TARGET is COACTUPC / COACTUP / CACTUPA from :1031-1033 and :3591-3592, and the termination is RETURN_TRANSID from :1015-1018 - never XCTL, because the only XCTL in this program is in the PF03 arm at :956-959 which this path does not reach. STATELESSNESS (rule R6, gate G37): every scrap of conversation state travels in the payload and none is held server side. Inbound it is the 1033-byte EIBCALEN, the AID, the sixteen carried CARDDEMO-COMMAREA fields and one received map field; outbound it is the sixteen navigation fields, where 9500 has replaced CDEMO-CUST-ID with 000000001, the three customer names, CDEMO-ACCT-ID with eleven zeros and CDEMO-ACCT-STATUS with a space from the unread record, while CDEMO-CARD-NUM keeps the 9680294154603697 the cross-reference supplied and CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT stays 1, and CDEMO-FROM-TRANID, -FROM-PROGRAM, -TO-TRANID, -TO-PROGRAM, -USER-ID, -USER-TYPE, -LAST-MAP and -LAST-MAPSET stay exactly as they arrived because only the PF03 arm at :944-950 writes them. NOTHING IS WRITTEN. COACTUPC's write verbs are the read-for-update and REWRITE pairs inside 9600-WRITE-PROCESSING at :3888-4105, which only the PF05 confirmation arm at :2602-2605 reaches, so expectedWrites is empty as a POSITIVE assertion and all three seeded datasets are pinned unchanged on the final-state channel as the other half of it. RETURN CODE 0: a CICS RESP is not a COBOL RETURN-CODE. COACTUPC never sets one - the identifier does not occur anywhere in its 4,236 lines - because it is pseudo-conversational and ends at EXEC CICS RETURN, so an unexpected RESP 19 produces a file-error MESSAGE and a normal step completion, not a non-zero exit. EXACTLY ONE MESSAGE. First-message-wins is the rule this folder's case14 pins, and it holds here for a different reason than usual: :2574 SET WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF, 9300's WHEN OTHER arm wrote the file-error text unconditionally at :3743, and 9400 succeeding adds nothing, so one text and only one reaches the screen. It is asserted where the program actually put it - in ERRMSGO at its declared 78, beside INFOMSGO at its declared 45 - and once on the SCREEN_ERRMSG_78 channel of expectedMessages, which is the channel named for exactly this truncation. There is no DISPLAY_LINE entry, because this path performs no COBOL DISPLAY and no SEND-PLAIN-TEXT, and no WS_MESSAGE_80 entry, because WS-FILE-ERROR-MESSAGE is a group item in COACTUPC's own WORKING-STORAGE and not the WS-MESSAGE PIC X(80) that channel is named for - the 80-byte value never reaches an emitter, which is the point of the truncation. TWO GATES ARE NOT APPLICABLE and are recorded as such rather than silently skipped. G32 does not apply: COACTUPC's fifty-one GO TOs all target an -EXIT label, COMMON-RETURN or a forward stage, and CBSTM03A is the only program in the migration whose GO TOs form implicit loops. G35 does not apply: CALL 'CEE3ABD' occurs zero times in COACTUPC - the nine sites are all in batch programs - and an unexpected RESP here produces a file-error message rather than an abend. The only abnormal exit this program has is the ABEND-ROUTINE at :4203-4226, whose EXEC CICS ABEND ABCODE('9999') at :4222-4224 is reached only from the WHEN OTHER of 2000-DECIDE-ACTION at :2633-2640, which case20 owns. G51 is honoured by unitKind CONTROLLER_POJO: account.AccountUpdateController is constructed directly with fixture-backed repositories and its handler called as a plain method - no MockMvc, no TestRestTemplate, no servlet container and no HTTP anywhere in the path. G15 and G18 place this case eighth of the twenty this program owns, and the module is not complete until the diff count is zero across all twenty. PROVENANCE (practice B12). Every expected value above was derived STATICALLY, by structured reading of the exact lines named - :40-43, :371, :389-408, :463-471, :479, :499-502, :573-582, :640, :866-868, :880-916, :921-1003, :1010-1018, :1031-1033, :1051-1062, :1433-1449, :1783-1817, :2562-2580, :2649-2661, :2698-2724, :2787-2864, :2955-2981, :3009-3015, :3171-3189, :3566-3581, :3591-3592, :3608-3644, :3650-3667, :3701-3746 with the nine spans of :389-408 measured span by span and summed to 80, and :3752-3765 - and by DECODING the named fixture rows against the named copybook offsets, CVACT03Y at 50 and CVCUS01Y at 500, cross-checked against the xxxI PICTURE clauses of app/cpy-bms/COACTUP.CPY, the DFHMDF definitions and INITIAL text of app/bms/COACTUP.bms, the commarea layout of app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy, the titles in app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy, the file definitions in app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD and the real data in app/data/ASCII/acctdata.txt, custdata.txt and cardxref.txt. It was NEVER captured from, recorded against or replayed from any execution of the legacy COBOL. Executing it is empirically impossible in this environment - no z/OS or CICS runtime, the available compiler reports its indexed file handler disabled, no Language Environment CEE* services exist, and DFHAID, DFHBMSCA and DFHATTR are absent from the repository - and this static derivation is the recorded substitute for an execution baseline, escalated as risk R-A of the migration plan rather than silently absorbed. Every record image and every screen value here is US-ASCII, named explicitly on the request and never taken from a platform default (practice B8); the clock is pinned to 2022-07-19T23:15:59, this source revision's own timestamp, so CURDATEO and CURTIMEO are fixed literals no wall clock can reach (practice B7); and every collection is ordered so a reader can follow it against the source (practice B7). No user-specified rule governs this fixture - review_rules returns exactly 'No user rules provided' - so the practices cited throughout are the enterprise-standard substitutes the migration plan records, not invented rules, and their absence is not treated as licence to assert less. TWO AUTHORING NOTES, recorded rather than resolved by invention. First, COACTUPCParityTest currently declares its twenty scenarios in Java rather than loading them from this directory and allocates its own case08 to a different scenario; the divergence in NUMBERING is recorded here because the scenario itself - the ACCTDAT WHEN OTHER arm and the message it truncates - is what this case is specified to pin. Second, case05's own prose describes case08 as owning the CXACAIX WHEN OTHER arm; this file's specification names the ACCTDAT site explicitly, which is why ERROR-FILE reads 'ACCTDAT' followed by two spaces and why 9300 rather than 9200 is cited throughout, and the discrepancy is stated here so no reader is misled by the sibling sentence.
